atlas-ch.0133: Probation is usually 1 month and can be extended to a maximum of 3 months by written agreement, with 7 days’ notice on either side. After it, notice is 1 month in the first year of service, 2 months in years 2 to 9 and 3 months after that, each to the end of a month (Art. 335c CO).
atlas-ch.0134: A 13th month salary is not required by law; it exists only where the contract, a collective agreement or the personnel rules provide for it. In 2024, 75.9% of employees received one, so check the contract.
atlas-ch.0135: Salary is usually settled in later interview stages rather than in the application; a job offer should come with a thorough employment contract, and a probation period must be agreed in writing.
atlas-ch.0136: Third-country nationals are admitted only if highly qualified, usually with a higher-education degree and several years of experience, and the employer must show that no suitable candidate is available in Switzerland or the EU/EFTA, with pay and conditions matching regional and sector norms.
atlas-ch.0137: Quotas cap how many can be admitted: 8,500 qualified third-country workers in 2026 (4,500 B and 4,000 L permits), of which employers used 74% in 2024 and about 52% by the end of September 2025.
atlas-ch.0138: What an employer wants to hear is that you already hold the right to work, or the exact basis on which you will: say it in the first message, because the test and the quota are the employer’s paperwork and cost time.
atlas-ch.0139: Boards: jobs.ch (German, French and English versions) for German-speaking Switzerland, jobup.ch for the French-speaking region, and talendo.ch for students and graduates, which also lists career fairs and networking events.
atlas-ch.0140: University services: HSG Career & Corporate Services (Career Days, Banking Days) for St. Gallen; the federal job portal Stellenportal Bund for federal internships.
atlas-ch.0141: Programmes to look up: UBS graduate talent programmes, Roche’s Operations Rotational Development Program, ABB’s Global Early Talent Program and Deloitte’s St. Gallen traineeship.
atlas-ch.0142: Applying from abroad without a right to work: the third-country test and quota make employers cautious, and internships in practice go to Swiss, EU/EFTA citizens or students at a Swiss university.
atlas-ch.0143: Arriving at the end of the master’s without practical experience: two-thirds of master’s graduates who struggled to find suitable work named insufficient experience, and at St. Gallen 95% had more than six months.
atlas-ch.0144: Writing in the wrong language or a long CV: write in the language of the advert, one A4 page for the CV, one page for the letter.
atlas-ch.0145: Treating the 13th month salary as automatic: it is not required by law, so confirm it in the contract.
atlas-ch.0146: In French-speaking Switzerland and Ticino, 45% of ads for business and social-science graduate roles ask for German; in the ads as a whole more than a third name two or more languages.
atlas-ch.0147: Private and cantonal banks want the local language of the region; global banking teams work in English. The study of ads gives German with English or French as the common pairs.
atlas-ch.0148: English is the second most named language in Swiss job ads (32%) after German (87%); in French-speaking Switzerland 49% of ads for technical specialists ask for German. The pages read give no tech-only split.
atlas-ch.0149: AI roles sit in ETH and EPFL labs and in the research centres of large tech firms in Zurich; no language level is stated on the pages read.
atlas-ch.0150: A year after graduating, unemployment was 6.4% for university master’s graduates (3.9% in 2023) and 4.9% for bachelor’s graduates of universities of applied sciences (3.4% in 2023); 0.7% for teacher-training graduates.
atlas-ch.0151: The share saying they had trouble finding suitable work rose from 30% to 44.1% for master’s graduates and from 24.2% to 36.9% for bachelor’s graduates of universities of applied sciences (classes of 2022 to 2024); in economics and business it was 43.9% and in engineering and IT 39.6% (university of applied sciences).
atlas-ch.0152: The state of the economy was named as a reason by 42.5% of master’s graduates in 2025, up from 23.8% in 2023.
atlas-ch.0153: EU and EFTA citizens work in Switzerland under the free-movement agreement, with no labour-market test or quota: a contract of up to 364 days gives an L permit, a longer or open-ended one a B permit valid five years.
atlas-ch.0154: Register at the commune within 14 days of arriving and before your first day of work; the receipt lets you start. Up to 90 days of work a year need only an online notice by the employer.
atlas-ch.0155: Take out Swiss basic health insurance within three months; it is charged back to your arrival. A student who does not work can be exempted with the European Health Insurance Card.
atlas-ch.0157: Apply for the D visa at the Swiss embassy three to four months before term, with admission, a study plan and a written undertaking to leave when you finish; the canton decides.
atlas-ch.0158: No paid work in the first six months; after that, 15 hours a week in term with cantonal approval, full time in holidays.
atlas-ch.0159: Switzerland does not follow the EU student-mobility rules: a student permit from an EU country gives no right to study here, even on an exchange.
atlas-ch.0160: Funds in a Swiss bank (by canton)
atlas-ch.0161: CHF 21,000 a year in Zurich; CHF 24,000 in Vaud, Geneva, Basel and St. Gallen
atlas-ch.0162: CHF 90 visa, CHF 95 entry approval, CHF 142 to 182 permit
atlas-ch.0163: The student health exemption ends the moment you take any paid work, even a few hours as an assistant: then Swiss insurance at the full premium is compulsory.
atlas-ch.0164: Up to 90 days a year the employer only notifies the job online; from 91 days to a year you register at the commune and get an L permit.
atlas-ch.0166: Only an internship your degree, Swiss or foreign, requires, up to half the length of the course: the company applies to the cantonal labour office with the university’s certificate. Internships after graduating are not allowed, except under the young-professionals agreements or within the job-search months after a Swiss degree.
atlas-ch.0167: Six months to look for work after a Swiss degree
atlas-ch.0168: After a Swiss degree you may stay six months to find a job; the employer must then show the hire is of preponderant scientific or economic interest to skip the priority for residents.
atlas-ch.0169: The hire still needs a place in the annual quotas: a bill to exempt Swiss graduates was shelved.
atlas-ch.0171: CHF 10,500 in Zurich, CHF 12,000 in Vaud, Geneva and Basel
atlas-ch.0172: Specialist or manager permit (B or L)
atlas-ch.0173: Only managers, specialists with a university degree and highly experienced professionals qualify; ordinary jobs are closed to non-EU citizens. The employer must show no suitable candidate was found in Switzerland or the EU/EFTA, and pay the local and sector rate.
atlas-ch.0174: The canton and then the federal migration office approve; a quota place is needed: 4,500 B and 4,000 L permits in 2026, with a separate 3,500 for UK citizens.
atlas-ch.0177: Swiss PhD students and postdocs are salaried staff; the university’s HR files the permit, and academic research enjoys easier admission, without the residents’ priority.
atlas-ch.0178: As employees they must join Swiss health insurance at the full premium.
atlas-ch.0182: There is no working-holiday visa. Instead, citizens of 14 countries, the UK and the US among them, aged 18 to 35 with a degree or vocational qualification, can work full time in their own field for up to 18 months, outside the quotas and with no residents’ priority.
atlas-ch.0183: Visits up to 90 days in any 180; any paid work, even for a day, needs prior cantonal approval for non-EU citizens.
atlas-ch.0185: Normally after ten years with a B permit, or five with good integration (B1 spoken, A1 written in the local language). Study years count only if followed by at least two years on an ordinary B permit.
atlas-ch.0186: EU and EFTA citizens usually get the permanent C permit after five years.
atlas-ch.0187: Line up housing that lets you register within 14 days: towns refuse registration on an Airbnb or hotel booking, and vacancy rates are 0.11% in Zurich and 0.31% in Geneva, so many newcomers book a serviced apartment first.
atlas-ch.0188: Once the canton approves, collect the D visa (90 CHF) before you travel; the permit fees in Switzerland are CHF 137 to 144.
atlas-ch.0189: Register with the residents’ office (Einwohnerkontrolle, contrôle des habitants) within 14 days of arriving and before your first day of work, with passport, lease or the main tenant’s accommodation statement, work contract or enrolment, 2 photos and civil-status papers. Working before registering counts as undeclared work.
atlas-ch.0190: The registration receipt (Meldebestätigung) lets you work and start other formalities while the biometric permit card is made, in 3 to 8 weeks.
atlas-ch.0191: With a work contract of a year or more you get a B permit valid 5 years.
